messages:
Sam: Heads-up: noticed a p99 spike on nightly load test after the kernel selector change. baseline p50/p95 fine, p99 up ~120ms.
Maya: ugh, saw that too. timeline? did it correlate with batcher config or kv misses?
Sam: spike starts ~2678900600 in the trace. profiler shows extra kernel fallback calls and a bunch of small microbatches (1-2 tokens). KV hit rate dropped ~8% around same window.
Liam: small microbatches + KV cold misses = more kernel handoffs, that can amplify tail. Any change to max_batch_tokens or wait?
Sam: we rolled kernel-selector v2 at 2678899000. scheduler config was tweaked (reduced max_wait_ms from 12 -> 6) to improve latency earlier this week.
Olga: That matches. Shorter max_wait reduces grouping, increases microbatch count. With kernel v2's fallback path slightly slower for small batches, p99 can move.
Maya: perf-bot, post the profiling summary?
perf-bot: perf summary: https://perf.internal/runs/2678901200 - breakouts: kernel_fallback_count +43%, avg_kernel_switch_latency +18ms, kv_miss_rate +8%, request_batched_size_median 1 -> 1, mean remains ~3. (see flame chart attached)
Liam: flame looks like two stalls: KV fetch + kernel reconf. I think we hit a tipping point where reducing max_wait_ms helped median but increased tail due to batching fragmentation.
Sam: proposal: revert max_wait_ms to 10 and add a short grace window for prefix aggregation: grace_period_ms=4. Increase max_batch_tokens from 2048 -> 3072 for this model family to allow slightly larger batches.
Olga: alternatively we could keep max_wait low but introduce a microbatch coalescer that waits up to micro_coalesce_ms for same-key requests (helps KV warmup). More infra work though.
Maya: quick experiment plan: A/B two configs on canary hosts: (A) restore max_wait_ms=10 + max_batch_tokens=3072 + grace=4; (B) keep max_wait_ms=6 + micro_coalesce_ms=5 + leave max_batch_tokens. Run 6h each and compare p50/p95/p99, kv_hit, kernel_fallback.
Liam: also add metric: kernel_fallback_per_microbatch and tail_latency_by_batch_size. Need to ensure we capture KV cold windows per-instance.
Sam: I'll push canary configs. Config snippets: ```
scheduler:
  max_wait_ms: 10
  max_batch_tokens: 3072
  grace_period_ms: 4
micro_coalesce:
  enabled: false
```
Maya: and for B: ```
scheduler:
  max_wait_ms: 6
  max_batch_tokens: 2048
micro_coalesce:
  enabled: true
  micro_coalesce_ms: 5
```
Olga: if A reduces p99 without harming p50/p95 and keeps throughput, prefer that as quicker fix. If throughput drops, we might need better kernel-tuning for small batches.
perf-bot: Canary jobs scheduled: canary-A(2678901260), canary-B(2678901270). Will report in ~6h.
Sam: Thanks. I'll also add a tail-sampling probe to capture KV miss stack traces for the p99 requests.
Maya: good call. also add sample prompts to reproduce small-microbatch pattern.
Liam: one more note: if kernel-selector v2 picks a slower pathway for short sequences, we should consider a threshold in selector: if batch_size <= 4 prefer kernel-v1 for now. That avoids regressions while we optimize v2.
Olga: agreed. Add a quick selector override toggle in rollout.
Sam: Logged follow-ups in tracker: INF-4821 (canary experiments), INF-4822 (selector short-batch override), INF-4823 (micro_coalesce RFC).
Maya: great. keep updates here once canary metrics land. :thumbsup:
